findings.title: The sync-mode schema discards the refreshed token fields
findings.body: In credential-sharing mode this schema accepts only `access_token` plus a computed property whose key is the stringification of a Zod schema; it does not require or preserve the provider's expiry field. Zod objects strip unrecognized fields by default, so parsing a normal response drops fields such as `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, `refresh_token`, and provider-specific data. Callers then persist incomplete credentials or assign undefined expiry values, causing token refreshes to fail or repeat. Define and preserve the actual required response fields for each integration.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh never makes the refreshed token usable
findings.body: This code persists the newly refreshed token, but then constructs the connection using `credentialKey.instance_url` and `credentialKey.access_token` from the original credential. The new access token and potentially changed instance URL are ignored, so Salesforce calls continue with the old token and fail after expiry. Build the connection from the parsed refresh response and the retained refresh token.

findings.title: The new Prisma update has no Prisma import
findings.body: This file now calls `prisma.credential.update` but does not import or otherwise define `prisma`. TypeScript/build will fail with an unresolved identifier, preventing the app-store package from compiling.

findings.title: Credential ID is sent as the syncing user's ID
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` interprets its third argument as a Cal.com user ID and sends it as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`, the credential row's primary key. The external sync endpoint will look up the wrong user and may return another user's tokens or fail to find the intended credential. Pass `credential.userId` instead; retain the credential ID only for the local database update.
